svg.title: The number of angular sectors and component choices is finite; summing their constants preserves uniformity. If the specified annular stage is empty, the term is zero and the same estimate holds. Otherwise its geometry is exactly the refined route already described. Since P n aγ n = (1 −2−γ)−1 < ∞, (CE11) proves summability of the integral norms of the complete annular terms. The eventual germ equality from (CE9), together with the proper-normal exceptional sets of Haar measure zero, identifies the pointwise sum almost everywhere with the unsliced component expression. To pass to its integral without any unproved domination, regard each annular term as an element of the Banach space L1(E; X). The sum of their L1 norms is finite, so they sum in L1 to an integrable function. Absolute integral-norm summability also gives their almost everywhere pointwise sum; uniqueness and the eventual identity identify that function with the prescribed unsliced expression.
